title: Uricosuric action of losartan via the inhibition of urate transporter 1 (URAT 1) in hypertensive patients
authors: Hamada T, Ichida K, Hosoyamada M, Mizuta E, Yanagihara K, Sonoyama K, et al.
followUp: 1 month of treatment, with single-dose clearance studies
population: 32 patients with hypertension given losartan 50 mg/day or candesartan 8 mg/day, and 9 patients with idiopathic renal hypouricaemia, 5 of them hypertensive, some carrying loss-of-function URAT1 (SLC22A12) mutations
funder: not read: the publisher page is not accessible and the PubMed abstract carries no funding statement.
result: Losartan lowered serum urate with a concomitant rise in the urate-to-creatinine clearance ratio, whereas candesartan altered neither. In patients with loss-of-function URAT1 mutations neither losartan nor the URAT1 inhibitor benzbromarone changed serum urate or fractional urate clearance, whereas both raised fractional urate clearance in patients carrying the wild-type gene; the authors conclude that losartan lowers serum urate by inhibiting URAT1.
